title: Garvie's Point Site
summary: The Garvies Point Site featured a once exposed archaic shell midden found on an eroding bluff. During 20th century excavations, among the objects found in the shell deposit were a semi-lunar knife or ulu of ground blue slate, a large slate projectile point, a broken chisel, and a bannerstone or atlatl weight, each from the archaic period. The site appeared to be pre-pottery characteristic of the archaic period.
address_label: Garvies Point Museum and Preserve, Glen Cove, New York (public museum area)
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Matinecock Traditional Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: Shell middens and Archaic-period tools at Garvie's Point place Native Long Island in deep time, through generations of Indigenous knowledge, coastal foodways, and careful use of local stone, shellfish, and shoreline environments. The lesson is also about protection: erosion, development, and collecting have damaged many coastal archaeological places. Learning from the public museum and preserve should build respect for Native continuity and for the responsibility to preserve what remains.
history_content: Public Museum and Shellfish Context Garvies Point is best understood through the museum and preserve, with interpretation focused on Long Island Algonquian archaeology, shellfish processing, and the protection of eroding coastal sites. The map points to the public museum and preserve area rather than sensitive archaeological deposits.
